title: Working with Images, Text, and TFRecords 📁
description: Efficiently load images from directories, text lines, and binary TFRecord files.

slides.title: Image Datasets from Directories 🖼️
slides.content:
# `image_dataset_from_directory`

Keras provides a convenient utility to load images from folders (each subfolder = class).

```python
train_ds = tf.keras.utils.image_dataset_from_directory(
    'data/train',
    image_size=(224, 224),
    batch_size=32,
    label_mode='int'
)
```
Returns a `tf.data.Dataset` of (image_batch, label_batch).

For large datasets, this may be I/O bound; you can combine with `.cache()`.

slides.title: Custom Image Loading with `map`
slides.codeSnippet:
def load_image(file_path, label):
    image = tf.io.read_file(file_path)
    image = tf.image.decode_jpeg(image, channels=3)
    image = tf.image.resize(image, (224, 224))
    return image, label

file_ds = tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices((file_paths, labels))
image_ds = file_ds.map(load_image, num_parallel_calls=tf.data.AUTOTUNE)

quizData.question: Which function reads the raw bytes of an image file?
quizData.explanation: `tf.io.read_file` reads the file contents as a string tensor; then `decode_jpeg` decodes it.

slides.title: Text Datasets 📝
slides.content:
# `TextLineDataset`

Reads each line of text files as a string tensor.

```python
text_ds = tf.data.TextLineDataset('corpus.txt')
text_ds = text_ds.filter(lambda line: tf.strings.length(line) > 0)  # skip empty
```
For multiple files, use `list_files` + `interleave` with `TextLineDataset`.

slides.title: TFRecord Format 📦
slides.content:
# Binary, Efficient Storage

TFRecord is TensorFlow's native format for storing sequences of binary records. Ideal for huge datasets.

Writing:
```python
with tf.io.TFRecordWriter('data.tfrecord') as writer:
    for example in examples:
        writer.write(example.SerializeToString())
```

Reading:
```python
raw_dataset = tf.data.TFRecordDataset('data.tfrecord')
parsed_dataset = raw_dataset.map(_parse_function)
```
The `_parse_function` decodes the protobuf using `tf.io.parse_single_example`.

slides.title: When to Use TFRecord 📂
slides.content: If you have millions of small files, combine them into sharded TFRecords for faster I/O and better shuffling.
